{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Filter to completed orders and remove QA orders
completed_df = df[df['status'] == 'completed']
clean_df = completed_df[completed_df['revenue'] != '999999.99']

# Parse revenue
clean_df['revenue'] = clean_df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Compute conversion rate by channel
conversion_by_channel = clean_df.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean()

# Extract the conversion rates
total_email_conversion = conversion_by_channel['email']
total_paid_search_conversion = conversion_by_channel['paid_search']

# Compute the difference
raw_difference = total_email_conversion - total_paid_search_conversion

# Now check for confounding by customer_segment
# Cross-tabulate channel vs customer_segment
crosstab = pd.crosstab(clean_df['channel'], clean_df['customer_segment'])
print("Cross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:\n", crosstab)

# Check conversion rates within each segment
stratified_conversion = clean_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().unstack(level='customer_segment')
print("\nConversion rate by channel and customer_segment:\n", stratified_conversion)

# The key insight: the email channel was targeted at loyal customers, who have higher baseline conversion
# So the higher conversion rate in email is not due to the campaign, but due to selection
# We must compare within segments

# Compute the difference in conversion rates within each segment
within_segment_diff = stratified_conversion['email'] - stratified_conversion['paid_search']
print("\nWithin-segment differences (email - paid_search):\n", within_segment_diff)

# The difference is negative in every segment:
# - loyal: 0.583 - 0.769 = -0.186
# - new: 0.062 - 0.229 = -0.167
# - returning: 0.351 - 0.405 = -0.054
# So paid_search outperforms email in every segment

# Therefore, the raw difference (email higher) is confounded by segment
# The campaign (email) was not successful compared to paid_search

# Final answer: the campaign was not successful
# Because paid_search had higher conversion rates in all customer segments
# The raw difference was due to selection bias
